machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.5 (bundled, static: linux-ext-libs 1.24); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-10-22, before the tag. 7.27.7 is the C code of the release: the main tree at 63d12373d (YUNETA_VERSION still says 7.27.6; the bump to 7.27.7 changes no C code). It is measured against 7.27.5, the last release with a study; 7.27.6, which changed .c files and shipped none, runs in the same rotation, so a move is placed in the release where it appears. The three each built from a git worktree, with the same .config and compiler; outputs_ext shared (linux-ext-libs 1.24 at all three). In each tree only the kernel libraries, the modules, performance/c/ and the three ctest binaries were built; the perf_timeranger2 of the main tree (with its `read` phase, public API only) was compiled into all three. The three binaries of each benchmark run in rotation, the order turned every round and reversed every third, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run (1 s for the three ctest binaries and the read phase): 8 rounds; 24 for perf_tr_treedb, the TCP and TLS echo and the event loop echo with an append (out of their noise, or at its edge, after 8); 48 for the `read` phase alone; perf_rotatory 16, its round 8 of 8 left out: something on the machine slowed the three builds alike for that minute (a log line 574 ns against 368 ns, on all three). An attribution build (7.27.7 with process_start_time() read once per process in remove_key_directory(), never shipped) ran perf_tr_treedb in the same rotation, 16 rounds. Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The treedb figures are CPU time of the process per operation.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.27.7 are its side of the A/B run: its C code (the main tree at 63d12373d, before the version bump), built on 2026-10-22 on the machine of the earlier reports. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second; reads page by page are the FORWARD pass. The binary sizes are those of the release build of the main tree at the same commit.

story.title: Yuneta 7.27.7: three reviews of retention, at the speed of 7.27.5
story.lead: 7.27.7 closes three reviews of the retention that 7.27.5 gave timeranger2: the bounds of an iterator on a replica whose numbering a purge moved, the order of a purge and the links of its feeds, a base read again after a failure that passes, the reads an rt_disk follower owes after running out of descriptors, the parts of a multi-key C_TRANGER iterator. None of it costs a read. Against 7.27.5, the last release with a study, on the same machine, 40 of the 41 figures stay inside their noise: the read path of the master and of a replica, the appends, the opens of a store, the treedb writes, the event loop, TCP and TLS. The one outside comes from 7.27.6, which shipped without a report: a forced treedb delete takes 21% more CPU (43.6 -> 52.8 us), because every deleted key is now moved out of `keys/` whole before it is removed, so a delete that fails half way never renumbers a key.

hero.text: figures inside their noise against 7.27.5, the read path of a replica among them (a page of 1 row 6.27 -> 6.31 us, +0.6%): the fixes of three reviews of retention cost no measurable time. The one outside, a forced treedb delete, is a price of 7.27.6, named below.

story.append_note: +0.5% against 7.27.5 (231,340): t = 0.8 over 8 rounds; nothing of the append path moved in 7.27.6 or 7.27.7
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built from the tree of each release (7.27.5, 7.27.6 and 7.27.7), the binaries run in rotation: 8 rounds, 24 for the four figures that left their noise or reached its edge after 8, 48 for the read path. The bars compare 7.27.7 with 7.27.5; a change inside its whisker is noise. Everything is on one axis: the change of the time an operation takes.

ab.reason: Since 7.27.6 (commit 503c23efb, the only C change of that release) every key a delete removes is first moved out of keys/ whole, by a rename(), and then removed. A removal that failed half way left part of the key's files; the key, read again from them, moved the rows after the hole, and its next appends took g_rowids that followers and clients had seen. 7.27.5 moved only a key with a base. Placed by the rotation: 7.27.5 43.6 us, 7.27.6 52.7 us, 7.27.7 52.8 us (+0.3% against 7.27.6, t = 0.8). An attribution build of 7.27.7 that reads the start time of the process once takes 47.7 us: about 5 us of the 9.2 us is process_start_time(), a read of /proc/self/stat made at every delete to name the moved directory, and about 4 us the rename. CPU time per delete.
